findings.title: Inverted ERC721 Receiver Check in safeTransferFrom
findings.description: The check `data != IERC721TokenReceiver.onERC721Received.selector` is backwards. Compliant receiver contracts (returning the correct selector) have their transfers reverted. Non-compliant contracts pass the check. This means `safeTransferFrom` is unsafe — it accepts transfers to contracts that don't implement the receiver interface and rejects those that do. NFTs sent via safeTransferFrom to correctly-implemented receiver contracts will always revert. NFTs sent to non-receiver contracts will succeed, potentially locking positions permanently.

findings.title: update_emergency_council Overwrites nft_manager Storage Slot
findings.description: The function update_emergency_council_7D0C1C58 executes self.nft_manager.set(manager) instead of self.emergency_council.set(manager). Any call to updateEmergencyCouncil7D0C1C58 silently overwrites the nft_manager address. Since nft_manager controls all position NFT transfers via transferPositionEEC7A3CD, this enables complete fund theft: (1) Admin calls updateEmergencyCouncil(attacker) which sets nft_manager = attacker, (2) Attacker calls transferPosition(id, victim, attacker) for any position, (3) Attacker drains all liquidity and fees.

findings.title: collect_protocol Token/Recipient Arguments Swapped
findings.description: Token and recipient arguments in collect_protocol_7540FA9F are transposed in the erc20::transfer_to_addr calls. The function signature is transfer_to_addr(token, recipient, amount) but the call passes (recipient, pool, amount), sending protocol fees to the token address instead of the intended recipient. Protocol fees are irrecoverably stranded every time collect_protocol is called.

findings.title: burn_position Allows Burning With Remaining Liquidity
findings.description: Positions can be burned via burn_position_AE401070 without removing liquidity first. There is no check that position liquidity is zero before erasing the position from storage. This permanently locks the tokens associated with the burned position's liquidity, as there is no way to recover them after the position record is deleted.

findings.title: Leo Reward Calculation Doesn't Use Last Claim Timestamp
findings.description: The reward calculation in collect_lp_rewards uses clamped_secs_since = clamped_timestamp - campaign_starting, measuring elapsed time from the campaign start, not from the user's last claim or vest time. position.timestamp is stored but never read in the calculation. This allows repeated full reward claims in successive transactions and late-entering users claiming rewards for the entire campaign duration. Campaign reward pools can be drained immediately by any participant.

findings.title: Leo Position Campaign Offsets Never Persisted
findings.description: Campaign offsets computed during collect_lp_rewards are never written back to storage. The local variable offset is incremented within the loop but position.offsets.setter(campaign_id).set(offset) is never called. This allows repeated claims of the same rewards across multiple transactions, as the offset resets to zero on every call.

findings.title: Leo calc_base_rewards Formula Inverted
findings.description: The formula in calc_base_rewards computes pool_lp * rewards_per_sec / our_lp instead of the correct our_lp * rewards_per_sec / pool_lp. Rewards are inversely proportional to position size — users with smaller positions receive more rewards than large LPs. Small dust positions can extract maximum rewards while large liquidity providers receive nearly nothing.

findings.title: Leo create/update Campaign Takes Wrong Token
findings.description: The campaign creation calls erc20::take(pool, extra_max) using the pool address instead of the token address specified for rewards (campaign_bal.token). Campaign creators deposit the wrong asset. Campaign reward tokens are never actually deposited, and reward distributions attempt to send tokens that were never received.

findings.title: Leo seawater.rs WASM Functions Panic in Production
findings.description: Multiple Leo-to-SeawaterAMM bridge functions in the wasm32 build path contain panic!("TODO"), crashing the WASM runtime on any invocation. Affected functions include tick_lower, position_liquidity, and collect_yield_single_to. Leo's fee collection, liquidity queries, and tick queries are all non-functional in production builds.

findings.title: Faucet sendTo Unchecked send Return Value
findings.description: The send() return value in Faucet.sendTo is captured in a bool variable _rc but never checked. If a recipient's receive() consumes more than 2300 gas or reverts, the ETH transfer silently fails and the loop continues. Recipients do not receive their expected gas tokens with no indication of failure.

findings.title: swap_2 Takes original_amount Not amount_in
findings.description: The two-hop swap function swap_2_internal_erc20 calls erc20::take(from, original_amount, permit2) where original_amount is the raw user input. However, the actual amount consumed by the first pool swap leg is amount_in, which may be less on partial fills. The user is overcharged with the excess never returned or accounted for.

findings.title: Fee Growth checked_sub Locks All Positions in Pool
findings.description: Fee growth calculations in get_fee_growth_inside and position update use checked_sub which returns an error instead of wrapping. Uniswap V3 intentionally relies on unsigned integer wrapping for fee growth tracking. When fee_growth_outside exceeds fee_growth_global (valid in the wrapping model), checked_sub fails, causing all position operations (update, collect, adjust) to revert for every position in the affected pool. This results in permanent DoS.

findings.title: set_sqrt_price Doesn't Update cur_tick
findings.description: The admin function set_sqrt_price changes the pool's sqrt_price but leaves cur_tick unchanged, creating a price-tick mismatch. This corrupts all subsequent swap calculations (which use cur_tick to find the next initialized tick) and fee distributions (which use cur_tick to determine which positions are in range).

findings.title: transfer_position Doesn't Verify from Is Owner
findings.description: The from parameter in transfer_position_EEC7A3CD is not validated against position_owners[id]. The function only checks msg.sender == nft_manager but accepts any arbitrary from address. This means remove_position is called on an address that may not own the position, corrupting ownership accounting.

findings.title: Leo create_campaign Checks Owner Before Setting It
findings.description: The ownership check in create_campaign occurs before the campaign is created, so the initial owner field is Address::ZERO. The check assert_or!(campaign_bal_owner == msg::sender()) fails for legitimate first-time creators (since Address::ZERO != msg::sender()). The access control logic has a bootstrapping contradiction that either blocks all campaign creation or allows unauthorized creation depending on the exact check implementation.

findings.title: swapOut Slippage Check Verifies Wrong Return Value
findings.description: swapOut5E08A399 checks require(swapAmountOut >= int256(minOut)) where swapAmountOut is the fUSDC input (amount_1), not the token output (amount_0). Users have zero slippage protection on the actual output token amount. Additionally, the price limit is set to type(uint256).max, providing no on-chain price bound.

findings.title: decrPosition Missing pool Param Causes ABI Selector Mismatch
findings.description: The Solidity decrPosition09293696 function takes 5 parameters but the Rust implementation expects 6 (including pool as the first parameter). The ABI selector mismatch between the Solidity interface and Stylus executor means the function is completely uncallable — any call will either revert or decode parameters incorrectly.

findings.title: OwnershipNFTs Emits Zero ERC721 Events
findings.description: No Transfer, Approval, or ApprovalForAll events are ever emitted in OwnershipNFTs. The _transfer function, approve function, and setApprovalForAll function all modify state without emitting the mandatory ERC721 events. All off-chain indexers, NFT marketplaces, and wallets will have permanently stale ownership and approval data.

findings.title: remove_position owned_positions Underflow Wraps to U256::MAX
findings.description: The subtraction owned_positions.get(owner) - U256::one() in remove_position has no zero-check. In WASM release builds, if owned_positions for an owner is already 0, the subtraction wraps to U256::MAX (2^256 - 1), permanently corrupting the balanceOf accounting for the affected address.

findings.title: Leo collect_pool_rewards Uses Wrong ABI Selector
findings.description: Leo's seawater.rs declares COLLECT_YIELD_SINGLE_TO_SELECTOR as [0xd2, 0xb3, 0x16, 0x5c] referencing non-existent function collectSingleTo720C50FF instead of the actual collectSingleTo6D76575F. When Leo's WASM build calls SeawaterAMM with this wrong selector, the call hits the fallback dispatcher where msg.data[0]=0xd2 fails the require(msg.data[0] == 0) check, causing a revert. AMM fee collection for Leo-vested positions is completely non-functional.

findings.title: burn_position on Leo-Held Position Corrupts Leo Accounting
findings.description: burn_position_AE401070 has no check for external protocol management. If an attacker gains nft_manager control (via VULN-002), they can transfer a Leo-vested position to themselves and then burn it. Leo's internal positions map still records the original user as owner with non-zero liquidity, but the position no longer exists in SeawaterAMM. Leo's pool liquidity counter remains inflated, and subsequent divest_position calls revert due to ownership mismatches.

findings.title: swapOutPermit2 Same Slippage Bugs as swapOut
findings.description: Variant of VULN-017 in the permit2 code path. swapOutPermit23273373B uses the same require(swapAmountOut >= int256(minOut)) pattern checking fUSDC input instead of token output, and the same type(uint256).max price limit providing no price bound. Users of the permit2 swap path have zero slippage protection.

findings.title: OwnershipNFTs approve() Checks Self-Referential Authorization
findings.description: The approve() function passes msg.sender as _from to _requireAuthorised, making the isApprovedForAll check evaluate isApprovedForAll[msg.sender][msg.sender] — a self-referential mapping lookup — instead of isApprovedForAll[tokenOwner][msg.sender]. Operators who are approved-for-all by the actual token owner cannot call approve() on behalf of the owner.

findings.title: ownerOf Returns address(0) for Non-Existent Positions
findings.description: The ownerOf function returns address(0) for non-existent position IDs instead of reverting, violating the ERC721 requirement that ownerOf throws for invalid token IDs. Protocols that check ownerOf to verify token existence will receive misleading results.

findings.title: create_position Missing low < up Tick Validation
findings.description: The create_position function validates that ticks are aligned to tick_spacing and within min/max bounds, but does not validate that tickLower < tickUpper. A position with tickLower >= tickUpper is economically invalid and could produce undefined behavior in fee growth and liquidity calculations.

findings.title: Leo divest With Empty Campaigns Loses Unclaimed Rewards
findings.description: divest_position zeros the position owner after collecting only the user-specified campaigns. If a user calls divest_position with an empty or incomplete campaign list, the owner is set to Address::ZERO, preventing any future collect_lp_rewards calls. Uncollected campaign rewards for campaigns not listed in the divest call are permanently lost.

findings.title: Fee Accumulation U256 to U128 Truncation Silently Loses Fees
findings.description: In position.update(), the fee calculation returns owed_fees as U256 from full_math::mul_div, but it is converted to U128 via U128::wrapping_from(owed_fees) which silently truncates the upper 128 bits. For positions with extremely high fee_growth_inside delta or very large liquidity, accrued fees exceeding u128::MAX are silently lost.

findings.title: tick.cross Unchecked Subtraction on Fee Growth
findings.description: The tick.cross function uses the bare - operator on U256 fee growth values (fee_growth_global - fee_growth_outside). In WASM release builds this wraps silently; in debug/test builds it panics. This is inconsistent with checked_sub used in get_fee_growth_inside (VULN-012). If fee_growth_outside exceeds fee_growth_global (possible after set_sqrt_price desync per VULN-013), the wrap produces corrupted fee_growth_outside values.

findings.title: Missing ERC165 supportsInterface Implementation
findings.description: OwnershipNFTs implements IERC721Metadata but provides no supportsInterface(bytes4) function. Any external contract or marketplace that calls supportsInterface to verify ERC721 compliance before interacting will receive a revert, treating the contract as non-ERC721 and preventing marketplace and protocol integration.

findings.title: updateExecutors/updateProxyAdmin Emit No Events
findings.description: The two most privileged admin functions in SeawaterAMM — updateExecutors (which can replace all seven executor contracts) and updateProxyAdmin (which can transfer full proxy control) — emit no events. There is no timelock, no event emission, and no external visibility into these admin operations, making silent admin takeovers undetectable through standard log monitoring.

findings.title: SQL Injection in snapshot/database.go storePositions
findings.description: Raw SQL is built via fmt.Fprintf(&bu, "'%s'", addr) string concatenation in storePositions, then executed directly with db.Exec(s). Pool addresses sourced from on-chain RPC responses are interpolated without parameterization. A malicious Ethereum node or corrupted database entry could supply a crafted pool address string to break out of the ARRAY literal and execute arbitrary SQL against the Postgres backend.

findings.title: Faucet Rate Limit TOCTOU Race Condition
findings.description: The rate-limit check (SELECT from faucet_requests) and the subsequent INSERT record creation are two separate, non-atomic database operations with no SELECT FOR UPDATE, advisory lock, or unique constraint enforcement. Under concurrent requests with the same wallet address or IP, multiple goroutines can pass the SELECT check before any has committed an INSERT, resulting in multiple payouts within the rate limit window.

findings.title: Faucet IP Rate Limit Bypass With Empty X-Forwarded-For
findings.description: When X-Forwarded-For header is absent, strings.Split("", ",") returns [""] (slice of length 1 containing empty string), not an empty slice. The guard len(ipAddrsSplit) == 0 at line 25 never triggers, and ipAddr becomes an empty string. The rate-limit query WHERE ip_addr = '' never matches real prior requests, so every request without the header bypasses IP-based rate limiting entirely.

findings.title: Leo collect_lp_rewards Computes Rewards But Never Transfers Tokens
findings.description: The collect_lp_rewards function iterates campaigns, computes reward amounts, updates the distributed counter, and pushes (token, amount) tuples to an owed vector — but never calls any token transfer function. The return value Ok(owed) is discarded by divest_position. The erc20::take and erc20::give functions in Leo's erc20.rs are also no-op stubs returning Ok(()). All LP reward tokens deposited via create_campaign are permanently locked with no withdrawal path. Users receive zero rewards despite accounting showing distribution.

findings.title: Leo tick_upper Returns I32::ZERO Silently on wasm32
findings.description: The wasm32 implementation of tick_upper in Leo's seawater.rs makes the correct RPC call to SeawaterAMM but discards the return value and unconditionally returns I32::ZERO. Every vested position reports tick_upper=0, corrupting reward eligibility checks in collect_lp_rewards. Unlike tick_lower and position_liquidity which panic!("TODO"), this function silently returns wrong data — a more dangerous failure mode.

findings.title: Leo update/cancel_campaign Use assert_eq! (Panic) for Authorization
findings.description: Ownership checks in update_campaign and cancel_campaign use assert_eq! instead of assert_or!, producing a Rust panic on authorization failure. In the wasm32 runtime, a panic causes the entire transaction to revert with an out-of-gas or execution-reverted error rather than a clean error code, consuming all remaining gas and making the failure mode indistinguishable from other catastrophic errors.

findings.title: No Fee Validation — fee >= 1_000_000 Causes Swap DoS
findings.description: There is no validation in pool::init that fee < 1_000_000. The swap math computes U256::from(1e6 as u32 - fee_pips). If fee_pips >= 1_000_000, the u32 subtraction wraps (in release/WASM builds) or equals zero. A pool initialized with fee >= 1_000_000 has permanently broken swap math: exact-out swaps revert with DenominatorIsZero, exact-in swaps produce zero output per step. The pool cannot be re-initialized.

findings.title: Fee-on-Transfer Token Accounting Mismatch
findings.description: The swap flow updates pool math state (liquidity, tick, fees) based on the computed take_amount before the token transfer occurs. For fee-on-transfer tokens, the actual amount received by the AMM contract is take_amount - fee, not take_amount. No balance-before/balance-after measurement exists. This causes the AMM's internal accounting to permanently over-represent the amount of tokens it holds, leading to insolvency when positions are withdrawn.

findings.title: Pool Creation Allows tick_spacing=0 Causing Division-by-Zero
findings.description: pool.init() does not validate that tick_spacing is non-zero. A pool created with tick_spacing=0 causes division-by-zero panics in create_position (low % spacing at pool.rs:78) and tick_math::get_min_tick(0) (MIN_TICK / spacing at tick_math.rs:94). The pool is permanently broken with no re-initialization path due to the PoolAlreadyInitialised check. Admin-only, no fund loss.

findings.title: adjust_position Uses Tick-Derived Price + Missing Upper Bound Check
findings.description: adjust_position computes the current sqrt price using get_sqrt_ratio_at_tick(cur_tick) instead of reading the actual stored sqrt_price. The actual pool sqrt_price lies between get_sqrt_ratio_at_tick(cur_tick) and get_sqrt_ratio_at_tick(cur_tick + 1). This produces a slightly different liquidity delta than the actual price would. Combined with no upper bound check (amount <= desired) in adjust_position_internal — which deviates from Uniswap V3's NonfungiblePositionManager that enforces both bounds — users adding liquidity can be systematically overcharged by approximately 1 basis point.

findings.title: incrPositionPermit2 Has No Rust Implementation — Function Unreachable
findings.description: The Solidity proxy declares and routes incrPositionPermit25468326E to the update_position executor, but no corresponding Rust function exists in the update_positions feature block. The internal infrastructure (adjust_position_internal accepts Option<Permit2Args>) exists but no external entry point passes non-None permit2 arguments. All calls to this function revert with selector not found. Users cannot use Permit2 for adding liquidity.

findings.title: enable_pool Does Not Verify Pool Is Initialized
findings.description: enable_pool_579_D_A658 can be called by authorised_enablers to enable any pool address, including ones never created via create_pool. There is no check that sqrt_price != 0. An enabled-but-uninitialized pool has tick_spacing=0 (amplifying VULN-043's division-by-zero), sqrt_price=0, and max_liquidity_per_tick=0, creating immediate DoS for any user interaction with that pool.
